headline: Grey wolves restore Yellowstone's ecosystem, beaver colonies flourish
meta_description: Since 31 grey wolves returned to Wyoming's Yellowstone in 1995, nine beaver colonies have thrived as willow forests recovered and erosion risks fell.

body:
In 1995, 31 grey wolves were reintroduced to Wyoming's Yellowstone National Park. Decades later, the ripple effects of that single act continue to reshape the landscape—nine beaver colonies are now thriving in the park, a sign of profound ecological recovery.

The story reveals how one species can unlock healing across an entire ecosystem. As wolves returned to hunt elk and other prey, vegetation patterns shifted. Willow forests, previously overgrazed and struggling, began to recover. With restored willow stands came the beavers, building colonies and creating wetlands that stabilize riverbanks and reduce erosion.

This cascade—wolves returning, plants recovering, beavers flourishing—demonstrates that nature's balance, once lost, can be restored. The nine colonies thriving in Yellowstone today are far more than a wildlife success: they are markers of an ecosystem slowly healing itself, one relationship at a time.
